transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan, Maya, Luis (Redwood); Ethan, Priya, Sara, Oliver (BrightLayer)
---
(00:00) Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick note, we've got 45ish minutes, we'll run through the SDK snippets maya prepared, then open for q's and next steps
(00:22) Priya: thanks Jordan, want to get straight to the structured output piece — we need reliable JSON schema so our downstream services dont break or require complex parsers
(00:35) Maya: totally, we built a couple examples — one is strict schema enforcement where the model is constrained to return strictly typed JSON, the other is a hybrid where you return JSON plus a best-effort parser field in case of hallucination
(00:50) Ethan: when you say "constrained" how do you enforce? is that on the Redwood side or in the SDK runtime? like are you running a validator post-response?
(01:12) Maya: good question, so there are two levers: 1) the SDK can do post-response validation and re-prompt or call a fixup tool; 2) Redwood's function-calling mode can do schema checks server-side and optionally reject or auto-correct based on confidence thresholds — currently our reference SDK does the client-side validate-and-retry flow
(01:40) Oliver: that client-side flow worries me — our mobile clients are thin, we prefer server enforcement inside our backend, less device churn
(01:55) Jordan: understood. for the POC we recommended running hosted for fast iteration but you can flip to Dedicated or Private later. Dedicated gives more predictable latency but is a higher base cost
(02:18) Sara: compliance question — if we run hosted, how does KMS work? we need to ensure keys are customer-managed for a subset of flows
(02:33) Luis: short answer: hosted supports envelope encryption; for customer-managed keys we'd likely discuss Private or a Dedicated configuration integrated with your KMS via cross-account role. i'll follow up with the security doc
(02:55) Priya: perfect, please include audit log retention options — our compliance team needs at least 2 years
(03:10) Jordan: noted. Maya, can you demo the SDK snippet for a function call? maybe show nested tool invocation — e.g., calling the formatting tool, then validation tool
(03:25) Maya: sure, i'm screensharing — code sample: SDK.call({ model: 'rwd-32b', functions: ["formatPatientRecord","validatePII"], onResponse: async (resp) => { // psuedo 
  if(!validateSchema(resp)) { await SDK.call("fixupTool", {badResp:resp}) }}})
(03:55) Ethan: nice, that looks... acceptable. how do you handle kv-cache between consecutive requests? our app chains calls and reuses context heavily
(04:12) Maya: we expose streaming + KV cache pinning. server keeps a session KVC, and you can pin tokens or prefix so subsequent calls reuse caches. this reduces per-token compute. there's a TTL configurable per session
(04:35) Priya: i'm worried about cost blow-up with long sequences — do you have batching suggestions?
(04:48) Maya: yes, Redwood Optimize recommendations: batch at the edge for similar requests and use prefix caching for repeated prompts, plus quantized variants for low-cost backstop models. for POC we can recommend batch sizes based on your request distribution
(05:10) Oliver: for function-calling, what about failure modes — if validatePII fails mid-sequence do you rollback or continue with degraded output?
(05:27) Luis: default is fail-fast and return an error object to the client. however we also have graceful-degradation path — fallback to smaller model and flag the payload
(05:45) Ethan: can we see an example of an error object in the transcript? like schema mismatch payload?
(05:52) Maya: shows sample: {error: "schema_mismatch", details: {expected: 'PatientRecord', found: 'Text', suggestions: ['call fixupTool']}} — the SDK will surface that and optionally auto-invoke the repair function
(06:15) (06:15) Priya: sounds good. let's talk about latency — our SLA needs 200-300ms p95 for short queries (<=64 tokens). is that feasible on hosted?
(06:34) Jordan: depends on load and model. rwd-32b on hosted typical p95 for 64 tokens is ~220-260ms under light load; under heavy load it can spike, which is why Dedicated with reserved GPU pools is recommended for strict SLOs
(06:55) Ethan: what about cold KV cache penalties?
(07:02) Maya: cold-start can add ~30-60ms if cache misses, but continuous pinned sessions reduce that. we can instrument to show distribution, we'll share micro-benchmarks
(07:20) Priya: please send the benchmarks — we need numbers to show to infra
(07:27) Jordan: yes — action item
(07:33) (07:33) Oliver: switching gears — structured output and schema validation: are you using JSON schema v7? v4?
(07:45) Maya: we currently use a custom lightweight schema that's close to JSON Schema draft-07 with typed fields. our validator supports required/optional, nested arrays, and custom format validators (like iso-date, patient-id). we also let you upload a schema to the model registry for stricter enforcement
(08:10) Ethan: any plan to support Protobuf? our backend is protobuf-first
(08:15) Luis: we can map schemas; typically customers POST-compile to JSON schema then run validation. protobuf support is on roadmap but not in the POC scope
(08:30) Priya: if we provide a schema, do you version it with model rollouts? we want to avoid regressions
(08:40) Maya: yes, you can pin schema versions per model variant. rollouts will respect pinned schema and there's a canary flow for schema compatibility checks
(09:00) Jordan: quick check on stakeholders — who needs access to the POC dashboard?
(09:05) Priya: product + infra + security — i'll send list after the call
(09:10) (09:10) Ethan: technical question — when SDK retries due to schema failure, do you count additional tokens for billing?
(09:23) Jordan: yes each invocation is billed; we recommend the SDK do local validation and only escalate to retry when necessary to reduce cost
(09:35) Ethan: that makes sense. another ask: we'd like to run an internal stress test — 1k concurrent shallow requests for 30 minutes — can you support that on staging?
(09:50) Maya: yes we can provision a temporary staging capacity, but we need the exact payload shape and expected token sizes. we'll also need to coordinate rate limits and monitoring endpoints
(10:12) Priya: we'll produce a sample payload and target QPS — action item for Ethan
(10:20) (10:20) Sara: security detail — are logs redacted by default? we don't want PHI in logs; retention controls please
(10:35) Luis: logs can be redacted and scrubbed. for hosted we replace probable PHI with hashes unless you opt-in for raw logs. Private deployment lets you retain raw logs internally and control retention policies
(10:58) Sara: KMS integration? how deep is the integration for Private mode? does it require on-prem HSM?
(11:10) Luis: Private supports cloud KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) via customer-managed keys and can also integrate HSM for on-prem. i'll attach the architecture doc
(11:30) Priya: quick product question — if validatePII is a tool call, can the tool be hosted inside our VPC? we prefer tools that touch raw data to stay behind our network
(11:45) Maya: yes — tools can be proxied, and in Private mode you can register internal tools with the control plane so function invocation happens over your private link
(12:02) Ethan: that helps. now on schema enforcement, what if the model returns partial arrays or mis-typed fields — do you attempt to auto-correct or force re-run?
(12:18) Jordan: configurable policy per route: reject, attempt-repair (call fixup tool), or best-effort coercion. for medical data we recommend reject or attempt-repair with strong audit trail
(12:40) (12:40) Priya: can you show an example of the 'attempt-repair' flow with the SDK?
(12:48) Maya: demo snippet: response = await SDK.call(...); if(!validateSchema(response)) { repaired = await SDK.call('repairTool',{payload:response}); if(validateSchema(repaired)) return repaired; else throw new SchemaError(repaired) }
(13:20) Oliver: in practice how often does the repair step succeed? any numbers?
(13:27) Maya: on our internal tests repair success is ~78% for minor mismatches, lower for hallucination cases. we'll share more detailed stats in the bench doc
(13:45) Ethan: do repairs count as additional billing? yes — understood. one more — for chained tool calls latency adds up; do you recommend moving some validation to sync checks in our backend instead of function calls?
(14:05) Jordan: yes, pushing deterministic validation out of the LLM and into your backend typically reduces cost and provides deterministic guarantees. use the LLM for fuzzy things and backend for deterministic checks
(14:30) Priya: timeline question — we're aiming for an internal demo the week of 2026-09-28; is that realistic?
(14:40) Jordan: yes, if we get SDK snippets and benchmark numbers this week and you run the latency test by 9/18, we can target a demo on 9/27-9/29
(14:55) (15:00) Ethan: ok will do, i'll coordinate with infra for the stress test
(15:07) Maya: small note — when you integrate the SDK, watch for noise in ASR of function names (naming collisions). use strict function identifiers rather than human-readable names
(15:25) Oliver: got it. also, can we set up role-based access in the console for data redaction controls?
(15:35) Luis: yes RBAC and SSO via SAML are available; i'll include the admin guide link
(15:45) Priya: and on cost — can you show a few scenarios: hosted with heavy burst vs dedicated monthly commit?
(15:55) Jordan: we'll send a cost comparison sheet — it's a quick model: hosted = lower startup but variable; dedicated = higher fixed but lower per-token at scale. we'll include an example for your expected qps and token sizes
(16:15) Ethan: perfect. two longer-term asks: protobuf support and tighter protobuf->model pipeline, and a requirement to support our internal observability traces attached to token-level events
(16:30) Maya: protobuf is on backlog; token-level tracing exists but attaching your trace IDs is possible via request metadata headers — we can show that in the integration guide
(16:50) Priya: any blockers to moving from hosted pilot to dedicated if POC goes well? procurement or security items?
(17:02) Luis: procurement needs standard terms; security needs SOC2 attestation and a KMS alignment. Dedicated contracts include SLA clauses; Private adds more compliance support but takes longer to provision
(17:20) Jordan: wrap-up — recap next steps and owners
(17:28) Priya: please include a concise checklist for security + infra to sign off rapidly
(17:35) Jordan: will do — sending summary + attachments. thanks everyone
(17:45) (17:45) Sara: thanks all
(17:50) Ethan: thanks
(17:55) Jordan: end call
